Guntha Bhasker vs The State Of Telangana on 2 November,

Author: K. Lakshman

entities.text: Guntha Bhasker vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Bench: K. Lakshman
 Honourable Sri Justice K. Lakshman
 I.A. No. 1 Of 2020
 In/And
 Criminal Petition No.5345 Of 2020
Common Order:
The Criminal Petition is filed under Section 482 Cr.P.C. to quash the proceedings in Crime No.241 of 2020, pending on the file of the Dharmaram Police Station, Ramagundam District against petitioner.
The petitioner is sole accused in the said Crime.

The offences alleged against him are under Sections - 270 and 273 of IPC.
2.
The petitioner has also filed I.A. No.1 of 2020 to return the seized material Amber Tobacco four (04) bags and V-1 Tobacco 4 bags.

3. The learned counsel for the petitioners as well as the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor would submit that the subject matter is squarely covered by a common order dated 27.08.2018, passed by the High Court of Judicature at Hyderabad for the States of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh in Crl.P.
No.3731 of 2018 and batch, and placed copy of the said judgment for perusal.

entities.text: High Court of Judicature at Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
4. Perused the common order dated 27.08.2018 in Crl.P. No.3731 of 2018 and batch, wherein a learned Single Judge of the High Court of Judicature at Hyderabad for the States of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh following the guidelines laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal1, held that the police are incompetent to take cognizance of the offences punishable under Sections 54 and 59 (1) of the Food Safety and Standards (FSS) Act, 2006,
investigating into the offences along with other offences under the provisions of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, and filing charge sheet is a grave illegality, as the Food Safety Officer alone is competent to investigate and to file charge sheet following the Rules laid down under Sections 41 and 42 of FSS Act, whereas, in the present case, the police have registered the crime for the offences under Sections - 270 and 273 of IPC.

entities.text: High Court of Judicature at Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the said proceedings in Crime No.241 of 2020 against the petitioner herein are contrary to the principle held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the above decision and, accordingly, the same are liable to be quashed.
5. A perusal of panchanama report discloses that the police have seized four (04) Amber gutka bags each containing 100 packets and V-1 four gutka bags each containing 50 packets.

As the proceedings are being quashed against the petitioner in the crime itself, the said seized property is liable to be Guntha Bhasker vs The State Of Telangana on 2 November, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127699009/
1 returned to the petitioner.

entities.text: Guntha Bhasker vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, I.A. No.1 of 2020 is allowed.

6. In view of the above submission, the present Criminal Petition is allowed of in terms of the common order dated 27.08.2018 in Crl.P. No.3731 of 2018 and batch, and the proceedings in Crime No.241 of 2020 on the file of the Dharmaram Police Station, . 1992 Supp. (1) SCC 335 Ramagundam District, are hereby quashed against the petitioner - accused.
Similarly, the Investigating Officer is directed to return the aforementioned seized property to the petitioner on proper identification and acknowledgment.
As a sequel, miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, in the criminal petition, shall stand closed.

Note:
Registry is directed to annex a copy of common order dated 27.08.2018 in Crl.P.
No.3731 of 2018 & batch (B/O.) Mgr Guntha Bhasker vs The State Of Telangana on 2 November, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127699009/
